title: Board Oversight of Fund Operations and Service Providers
summary: A ten-module programme giving fund directors the tools to oversee fund operations and service providers, from NAV production and custody to errors and resilience.
intro: This training programme equips fund and management company directors to oversee the operations behind a fund, from NAV production and transfer agency to custody, audit and technology, and to hold service providers to account.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give fund directors a clear, practical view of how a fund's operations actually run, where they break and which service provider is responsible at each step. Participants leave able to read operational reporting critically, challenge service providers and management, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors and auditors.
sections.What It Covers: The service provider map, fund administration and NAV production, transfer agency and investor services including AML, valuation, financial statements and audit, depositary and custody oversight, portfolio management oversight, distribution and product oversight, operational risk, resilience, technology and AI, and errors, breaches and service provider reviews.
Intended Audience: Independent and non-executive directors of investment funds and fund management companies
Executive directors, designated persons and senior managers responsible for operations and delegate oversight
Company secretaries, governance leads and service provider relationship managers supporting fund boards
Learning Objectives: Explain who does what across the fund's operating model and where accountability sits
Identify the key process flows, break points and risk areas in administration, transfer agency and custody
Challenge valuation, financial reporting and audit outcomes with confidence
Oversee portfolio management, distribution and product governance without straying into management
Evaluate operational risk, resilience, technology and AI arrangements across the service provider chain
Apply a structured approach to errors, breaches and periodic service provider reviews
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about two hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two- to three-day programme or as a series of board briefing sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with process maps, case studies and a board question set, and modules can be selected or tailored to the fund range and service model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience as a fund director or in fund management or servicing is helpful. No operational or accounting specialism is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
Basel Committee, Principles for Operational Resilience (2021)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)

modules.title: Who Does What: The Fund Service Provider Map
modules.summary: An end-to-end map of a fund's operations, the parties that perform each activity and the contractual and regulatory lines of accountability back to the board.
objectives: Map the fund's key operations to the service providers that perform them
Distinguish delegation, outsourcing and sub-delegation and their implications for the board
Identify where operational accountability ultimately rests
syllabus: The fund operating chain: manager, administrator, transfer agent, depositary and distributors
Delegation, outsourcing and sub-delegation chains
Service agreements, service level schedules and key performance indicators
A board question set for understanding the operating model

modules.title: Fund Administration and NAV Production
modules.summary: How a net asset value is produced each dealing day, the process flow from trade capture to publication, and the break points and controls the board should understand.
objectives: Explain the fund accounting and NAV production process step by step
Identify the key risk areas and controls in the NAV cycle
Interpret administrator reporting and controls reports
syllabus: Trade capture, reconciliations, pricing, accruals and fee calculations
NAV review, sign-off and publication
Common break points: stale prices, corporate actions and late trades
Controls reports and what they do not cover

modules.title: Transfer Agency, Investor Services and AML
modules.summary: The operational mechanics of investor dealing and the register, the anti-money laundering obligations attached to them, and how directors oversee investor-facing operations.
objectives: Explain subscription, redemption and register maintenance processes
Assess investor due diligence, screening and suspicious activity controls
Oversee investor service quality, complaints and dormant accounts
syllabus: Dealing cycles, cut-off times, late trading and market timing controls
Investor due diligence, sanctions screening and suspicious activity reporting
Reliance on distributors and intermediaries for investor identification
Complaints, unclaimed proceeds and investor communications

modules.title: Valuation Oversight in Practice
modules.summary: The difference between calculating a NAV and valuing the fund's assets, how the valuation operating model works, and how boards gain assurance on hard-to-value positions.
objectives: Distinguish NAV calculation from the valuation of underlying assets
Evaluate the valuation operating model and the choice of calculation agent
Challenge fair value judgements and price overrides
syllabus: Valuation policy, pricing hierarchy and independent price verification
Selecting and overseeing the calculation agent and pricing vendors
Fair value accounting and level three assets
Price challenges, overrides and valuation committee reporting

modules.title: Financial Statements and the External Audit
modules.summary: How to read a fund's financial statements, what the external audit does and does not provide, and the board's role in the audit cycle.
objectives: Interpret the key components of fund financial statements
Explain the audit process, audit opinions and management letters
Oversee the auditor's appointment, independence and findings
syllabus: Statement of net assets, income statement, portfolio and notes
The audit cycle: planning, fieldwork, findings and sign-off
Modified opinions, emphasis of matter and management letter points
Auditor independence, rotation and non-audit services

modules.title: Depositary and Custody Oversight
modules.summary: The depositary's safekeeping, cash monitoring and oversight duties, the custody and prime broker models behind them, and how the board builds an effective relationship with the depositary.
objectives: Explain how custody risk varies by asset type, location and use of assets
Assess custody, sub-custody and prime broker models and their insolvency risks
Use depositary reporting to strengthen board oversight
syllabus: Safekeeping, record-keeping, cash flow monitoring and oversight duties
Custody chains, prime brokers, rehypothecation and insolvency risk
Cash, financial instruments and other assets: differing risk profiles
Depositary reports, escalations and liability for loss

modules.title: Portfolio Management Oversight
modules.summary: How the board oversees the investment process and compliance with investment restrictions without making investment decisions, using internal limits and escalation triggers.
objectives: Evaluate the key components of the portfolio management function
Set internal risk limits and escalation triggers ahead of prospectus limits
Interpret performance, risk and investment compliance reporting
syllabus: Investment process, mandate and risk budget
Pre-trade and post-trade compliance monitoring
Internal limits that trigger before a prospectus breach
Performance attribution, style drift and peer comparison

modules.title: Distribution and Product Oversight
modules.summary: The distribution life cycle from the investor's and the product's perspective, and how the board oversees who is buying the fund, what they are buying and how it is sold.
objectives: Explain the board's role in distribution strategy and distributor oversight
Apply product governance questions before launch, during the fund's life and at closure
Assess distribution data, marketing materials and value for investors
syllabus: Distribution models, platforms and bipartite versus tripartite agreements
Target market, stress testing and product reviews
Distribution data: who is buying, through which channel and why
Marketing communications and value for investors

modules.title: Operational Risk, Resilience, Technology and AI
modules.summary: How operational risk is identified and managed across the service provider chain, how operational and digital resilience is tested, and how boards oversee new technology including AI.
objectives: Describe an effective operational risk framework for the fund and its delegates
Evaluate cyber, third-party and supply chain resilience
Appraise the opportunities and threats of technology and AI in fund operations
syllabus: Risk and control self-assessment, risk registers and operational risk appetite
Operational and digital resilience: important services, impact tolerances and testing
Supply chain security, third-party concentration and exit plans
Transformation programmes and AI as both asset and threat

modules.title: Errors, Breaches and Service Provider Reviews
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around error and breach management, investor compensation and the periodic review of service providers, closing with a board oversight plan.
objectives: Apply materiality thresholds and correction policies to NAV errors and breaches
Oversee root cause analysis, investor compensation and regulatory notification
Design a risk-based programme of service provider reviews
syllabus: NAV errors, investment breaches and materiality thresholds
Root cause analysis, compensation and notification to the authority
Due diligence visits, scorecards and annual service reviews
Workshop: the board's operational oversight plan

related.title: Alternative Investments for Fund Directors
related.summary: An eight-module programme explaining hedge fund, private markets, real asset, structured and digital asset strategies to fund directors, with board questions on valuation, liquidity and fees.

related.title: Fund Board Governance Toolkit: A Risk-Based Oversight Workshop
related.summary: A six-module practical workshop giving fund directors a risk-based governance toolkit, from skills matrices to escalation triggers, and a draft oversight plan for their own board.

related.title: Investment Fund Governance for Directors
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund directors the tools to oversee delegates, manage conflicts, protect investors and evidence effective governance to supervisors.

related.title: Overseeing Regulatory Change: Annual Update for Fund Directors
related.summary: A six-module annual CPD update for fund directors on the year's regulatory developments and on overseeing regulatory change and regulatory risk.

related.title: Risk Oversight for Fund and Management Company Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving fund and management company directors the tools to oversee investment, operational and emerging risks and challenge the risk function.

related.title: AI Governance for Boards
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving boards and directors the understanding and tools to govern AI responsibly and evidence sound oversight to regulators.
